Convalesce

kon-vuh-LES · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To convalesce is to recover health and strength gradually after an illness or injury.

After the marathon left him dehydrated and exhausted, the runner spent two full days convalescing before he could even climb the stairs at home.

Worked Example

The old sea captain convalesced for months in a cramped ship's cabin after the storm nearly claimed his leg, refusing to let the surgeon amputate.

Convalesce covers the whole slow stretch of healing, not a single moment of getting better.

How Convalesce Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

recuperate

recuperate: to recover health and strength

heal

heal: to become healthy again

Antonyms

relapse

relapse: to become sick again after improving

deteriorate

deteriorate: to become progressively worse

How Strong Is It? — rest → convalesce → rehabilitate

rest vs. convalesce

rest vs. convalesce: Rest is simply pausing activity, without necessarily meaning someone is actively recovering from illness the way convalesce implies.

rehabilitate vs. convalesce

rehabilitate vs. convalesce: Rehabilitate goes further than convalesce, often involving active therapy to restore lost function, not just quiet recovery time.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: thoroughly, completely (intensifying) (Latin)

root — valesce

root — valesce: to grow strong, become well (Latin valere, 'to be strong')

Put it together

Put it together: Convalesce comes from Latin con- (intensifying) plus valescere ('to grow strong'), from valere ('to be strong') -- the same root behind the everyday word valid.

Use the root in a new word: valid

Use the root in a new word: valid: The referee ruled the last-second goal valid after reviewing the replay.

Root Check

Word Choice

Convalesce almost always describes a deliberate period of rest set aside specifically to heal -- it's a gentler, slower word than simply saying someone 'got better.'
